subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: On what date did the armistice ending the fighting on the Western Front come into effect?
questions.explain: The armistice came into effect at 11am on 11 November 1918.

questions.q: What was the total figure eventually set for German reparations after the Treaty of Versailles?
questions.explain: Reparations were fixed at 6.6 billion pounds in 1921, a sum Germans deeply resented.

questions.q: The AQA 'Conflict and tension' topic covering the First World War spans which years?
questions.explain: The AQA specification covers conflict and tension from 1894 to 1918.

questions.q: The 1916 Battle of Verdun was fought between Germany and which other country?
questions.explain: Verdun in 1916 was a prolonged battle of attrition between Germany and France.

questions.q: What military restriction did the Treaty of Versailles place on the size of the German army?
questions.explain: The German army was restricted to 100,000 men under the Treaty of Versailles.

questions.q: At the 1938 Munich Agreement, which territory was handed over to Germany?
questions.explain: The Munich Agreement of 1938 gave Germany the Sudetenland region of Czechoslovakia.

questions.q: On which date did the major British offensive at the Battle of the Somme begin in 1916?
questions.explain: The Battle of the Somme began on 1 July 1916, with nearly 60,000 British casualties on the first day.

questions.q: Which 1914 battle halted the German advance and led to the entrenchment of the Western Front?
options: The First Battle of the Marne
questions.explain: The First Battle of the Marne in September 1914 stopped the German advance and began trench warfare.

questions.q: What was the name of the German plan to defeat France quickly before turning to fight Russia?
questions.explain: The Schlieffen Plan aimed to knock out France via Belgium before Russia could fully mobilise.

questions.q: Which economic event of 1929 severely weakened the League of Nations' ability to act in the 1930s?
options: The Wall Street Crash and Depression
questions.explain: The Wall Street Crash of 1929 triggered a global Depression that fuelled aggression and weakened cooperation.

questions.q: In which year did the United States enter the First World War on the side of the Allies?
questions.explain: The USA entered the war in 1917, boosting Allied manpower and resources.

questions.q: The League of Nations failed to stop which 1931 act of aggression in the Far East?
options: The German remilitarisation of the Rhineland
questions.explain: The Japanese invasion of Manchuria in 1931 exposed the League's weakness.
